description: Live end-to-end testing of PI Agent session persistence

tests.name: Fresh session
tests.description: Create new session, remember secret word ZEBRA, reply with OK
tests.command: pi --session-dir "$SESSION_DIR" -p "Remember this secret word: ZEBRA. Reply with the word OK."

tests.name: Same-session continue
tests.description: Continue in same session, recall secret word ZEBRA
tests.command: pi --session-dir "$SESSION_DIR" -c -p "What secret word did I tell you? Reply with the word only."
tests.notes: Memory persistence verified across -c continue flag

tests.name: Storage check
tests.description: Verify session files exist in storage directory

tests.name: Ephemeral session
tests.description: Create ephemeral session with --no-session, verify no file created
tests.command: pi --session-dir "$SESSION_DIR" --no-session -p "Hello, will you remember this? Reply with the word HI."
tests.notes: Ephemeral mode successfully prevents session persistence

tests.name: Resume by ID
tests.notes: Session ID partial match works correctly

tests.name: Fork session
tests.description: Fork existing session, create new branch

tests.name: Export session to HTML
tests.description: Export session JSONL file to HTML format
tests.notes: Export generates viewable HTML transcript of session

tests.name: Project session default location
tests.description: Session created in default project directory without explicit --session-dir
tests.command: cd /Users/ricardo/Workshop/GitHub/agent-pi && pi -p "Reply with ONE word: OK."

key_findings: Session persistence works reliably across multiple invocations
Memory (ZEBRA word) persists correctly in session history
Session file format is JSONL (JSON Lines) with ISO timestamp + UUID
Ephemeral sessions (--no-session) work correctly, no files written
Session resumption by ID prefix works correctly
Fork creates independent session branch with full history
Export to HTML generates readable transcripts
Default project session directory uses escaped path format (--dashes--)
